claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the Provider support policy page linked from the support index).
Pulumi's Provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Pulumi's Provider support policy page describes which providers get long-term security updates (some Pulumi providers receive long-term security updates).
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists and lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Pulumi provides no patches at all for older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers (beyond the latest major and the LTS previous major).
The Pulumi Registry at /registry/ lists the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving long-term support are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Registry pages exist at /registry/packages/ for aws, azure, azure-native, azuread, command, docker-build, gcp, kubernetes, tls, vault.

The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs in the provider's code or direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.
A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtimes.
LTS provider releases remain compatible with the Pulumi engine version they were frozen at unless security fixes require otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.
When major N+1 ships, the old N becomes the LTS major and the previous LTS major reaches end of life the same day regardless of remaining 12-month window.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
LTS provider releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning is recommended.
Older majors (N-2 and earlier) receive no patches and are end of life.
The current major (N) receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions.
The FAQ page /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ has a section 'what-are-the-best-practices-for-maintaining-provider-versions'.
Pages /registry/ and /docs/support/getting-support/ exist.
